claims.text: Increasing the concentration of rare-earth elements in magnetic high-entropy alloys increases magnetic anisotropy.
Rare-earth-induced enhancement of magnetic anisotropy leads to higher coercivity.
A magnetic high-entropy alloy with increased rare-earth concentration will have a significantly higher coercive field than a matched alloy with the baseline rare-earth concentration.
The predicted coercivity increase should occur when the compared alloys receive the same processing and are tested at room temperature.
The coercivity-enhancing effect should hold over a range of rare-earth concentrations.
The coercivity-enhancing effect may saturate at very high rare-earth concentrations.
The exact relationship between rare-earth concentration and coercivity is not fully established.
